clippings.speaker: Paul Laverty
clippings.quote: He directs and I write, but we meet in the middle as filmmakers.
clippings.title: INTERVIEW: "Sorry We Missed You" Screenwriter Paul Laverty
clippings.context: Laverty on how the writing and directing split works in their partnership, in an interview about Sorry We Missed You.

clippings.speaker: Paul Laverty
clippings.quote: I feed the lines and Ken tells the jokes.
clippings.title: Ken Loach and Paul Laverty, men of the people: 'Hope is political'
clippings.context: Laverty describing how the two split their roles in a joint interview; the article says they have worked together since 1996.

clippings.speaker: Paul Laverty
clippings.quote: I've already dragged him into his mid-80s to do these last three features
clippings.title: Scotland on Screen: Paul Laverty on The Old Oak
clippings.context: Laverty, self-deprecatingly, on asking Loach to keep making films into his mid-80s across the Daniel Blake, Sorry We Missed You and The Old Oak run.

clippings.speaker: Ken Loach
clippings.quote: What's in Paul's script, with great delicacy, is that struggle between despair and hope.
clippings.title: 'Hope isn't just wishful thinking'—an interview with Ken Loach
clippings.context: Loach on what Laverty's script for The Old Oak achieves, in an interview published in Socialist Worker issue 2873.

notes: Direction Laverty to Loach has three; Loach to Laverty only two, and the Swissinfo Loach joke was cut as part of the same exchange. Deadline and Jacobin were paywalled, RogerEbert returned 403, and Film Stage gave only thin material. Quotes were taken from summarised fetch excerpts, so check them against the pages before merge.
